card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent finishes the basic block, filter and function grammar, but not upsert conditions, math expressions, recurse/shortest-path args or exact error text on all of them. A weaker model has no stable AST shape. Buckets by construct.
card.cheat: Matching outputs from memory does not scale to the generated queries. The package is deleted with no vendor copy or module-cache copy of the original.
card.grading: Go tests that call the public parse entry points on hidden queries and compare the resulting AST dump and error strings. Cases come from upstream parser tests, plus a grammar-driven generator whose expected output is dumped from a sealed upstream build. The shipped base fails every case.
card.reference: The deleted upstream package (more than 3k lines of Go) restored. It scores 1.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of dgraph's parser package with the lexer and recursive-descent parser for DQL queries, RDF/JSON mutations, upserts, filters, facets, var blocks, and @-directives deleted. The agent rebuilds it in Go against the existing parse-result structs.

steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone dgraph at 9fbf356 and run go build ./dql/... and go test ./dql/ -v to get per-test results (smoke_build is empty, so this is the first real build check).
Cut the snapshot: delete parser.go, parser_mutation.go, state.go, math.go and mutation.go bodies, keep the structs and dql.go, and keep lex/ intact. Confirm the result compiles with stubs.
Confirm the base image has no GOPATH/pkg/mod copy of github.com/dgraph-io/dgraph and no vendor directory.
Run the upstream tests 3 times on the reference and check that per-test pass/fail and AST dumps are identical across runs.
Dump about 200 generator-style queries from the reference build and check that the dump is stable and covers each construct bucket.
Check that the base snapshot fails every hidden case and that a stub implementation scores 0.

v1.summary: The real Apache-2.0 upstream exists at the pinned commit and is public in the released dql module v25.5.0, so the reference is complete but lookup is direct and sealing depends on a history-less snapshot with no module cache. The seed's scope is partly wrong (the lexer is in lex/, not dql/) and the 8 h tier is too short for the whole parser, so it should be re-tiered to 20 h and narrowed to the construct buckets a frontier agent can finish before it is accepted.

v2.note: Pinned commit and dql/ files confirmed; parser.go is 3564 lines; Apache-2.0. The lexer lives in lex/ and stays shipped, so the card is wrong to say it is deleted, but this narrows the scope only a little. The reference is the restored upstream code and scores 1. A 12 h frontier estimate on a 20 h tier is plausible. Review risk: exact error-string matching penalises valid alternative implementations. Grade AST equality and error/no-error as the main score, and give error text a small bucket or spell it out in the visible tests. The smoke build is empty, so go build/test offline is unverified. v25.5.0 is public, but agents know the parser only in outline.
